title: Bài sưu tầm 230 - Passage 2: The Price of Pleasure: How Cost Shapes Perceived Quality
passageHtml:
READING PASSAGE 230

The Price of Pleasure: How Cost Shapes Perceived Quality

Paragraph 1. Classical economic theory rests on a reassuring assumption: shoppers inspect a product's objective quality first, then decide whether the asking price is fair. Yet behavioural researchers have repeatedly shown that the arrow often runs in reverse. Rather than acting as a neutral summary of value, a high price tag actively alters how much enjoyment a person derives from the item itself.

Paragraph 2. To verify whether this distortion reflects polite social flattery or genuine sensory change, neuroeconomist Dr. Hilke Plassmann placed volunteers inside a brain scanner while they sampled five wines through tubes. Unknown to the participants, two pairs of samples were chemically identical, differing only in the price flashed on a screen beforehand—for instance, $5 versus $45, or $10 versus $90. Not only did volunteers rate the supposedly expensive pours higher, but scans revealed heightened activity in the medial orbitofrontal cortex, a region linked to real pleasure. Belief in cost had physically reshaped taste perception.

Paragraph 3. This 'marketing placebo effect' reaches well beyond luxury dining. In a medical trial, volunteers suffering mild electric shocks were given identical pain-relief capsules priced at either $2.50 or a discounted $0.10; eighty-five percent of the full-price group reported noticeable relief, compared with barely sixty percent in the bargain group. However, expectation has clear limits. Subsequent studies found that seasoned wine critics resisted price illusions far better than casual drinkers, and the effect faded rapidly when volunteers were told beforehand that labels might be misleading.

Paragraph 4. In online retail, similar psychological shortcuts are exploited through artificial urgency rather than high prices alone. Travel booking platforms frequently flash alerts such as 'only two seats left' or ticking countdown clocks, triggering mild anxiety that cuts short careful price comparison. Consumer watchdogs auditing major e-commerce portals recently discovered that many countdown timers simply reset to zero when the page was refreshed, exposing fabricated scarcity rather than genuine inventory limits.

Paragraph 5. Legal scholars note that banning luxury branding altogether would be unrealistic, since social prestige has always formed part of what buyers willingly purchase. Instead, European regulators are targeting deceptive interface cues, demanding that digital merchants prove stock warnings reflect real warehouse figures before displaying them to hurried shoppers.

groups.instructions:

groups.title: Questions 19–23
groups.instructions: Do the following statements agree with the claims of the writer in Reading Passage 230? In boxes 19–23 on your answer sheet, write YES, NO or NOT GIVEN.

groups.title: Questions 24–26
groups.instructions: Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D. Write the correct letter in boxes 24–26 on your answer sheet.

steps: Đoạn 1: "alters how much enjoyment a person derives" ↔ actual enjoyment (D).
Đoạn 2: "heightened activity in the medial orbitofrontal cortex" ↔ regions of the brain (A).
Đoạn 3: Thuốc giảm giá từ $2.50 xuống $0.10 làm tỷ lệ người thấy đỡ đau giảm từ 85% xuống 60% ↔ reduced perceived effectiveness (G).
Đoạn 4: "cuts short careful price comparison" ↔ discourage calm comparison (B).
Đoạn 5: "prove stock warnings reflect real warehouse figures" ↔ verify the accuracy (F).

q19.text: Consumers consistently evaluate an item's objective quality before considering its price.

steps: Đoạn 1: Kinh tế cổ điển giả định vậy nhưng nghiên cứu hành vi chỉ ra chiều ngược lại: giá cao làm thay đổi cả cảm nhận chất lượng.
Kết luận: Chọn NO.

q20.text: Professional wine critics scored the five wines identically regardless of the price displayed in Plassmann's scanner experiment.

steps: Đoạn 2 & 3: Có nhắc thí nghiệm máy quét của Plassmann và có nhắc giới phê bình rượu chuyên nghiệp ít bị đánh lừa ở các nghiên cứu sau, nhưng không hề nói giới phê bình rượu đã tham gia thử nghiệm máy quét của Plassmann và chấm 5 loại rượu giống hệt nhau.
Kết luận: Chọn NOT GIVEN.

q21.text: Warning participants in advance that price tags could be inaccurate weakens the placebo pricing bias.

steps: Đoạn 3: "the effect faded rapidly when volunteers were told beforehand that labels might be misleading."
Kết luận: Chọn YES.

q22.text: Countdown clocks on travel websites always correspond to genuine drops in remaining room availability.

steps: Đoạn 4: Nhiều đồng hồ đếm ngược tự reset về 0 khi tải lại trang — tức là khan hiếm giả tạo (fabricated scarcity).
Kết luận: Chọn NO.

q23.text: Legal experts consider a complete ban on high-priced status goods to be impractical.

steps: Đoạn 5: "Legal scholars note that banning luxury branding altogether would be unrealistic..."
Kết luận: Chọn YES.

q24.text: What was the main purpose of Dr. Hilke Plassmann's brain-scanning experiment?
options: A. to measure how quickly volunteers recognized luxury wine brands
B. to test whether higher prices encouraged volunteers to lie in surveys
C. to determine if price expectations altered actual neural pleasure responses
D. to compare how the brain reacts to cheap versus expensive medicines

steps: Đoạn 2: Nhằm kiểm tra xem đó chỉ là lời khen xã giao (polite social flattery) hay thực sự làm thay đổi cảm giác thần kinh (genuine sensory change).
Kết luận: Chọn C.

q25.text: Why do online booking platforms display messages such as 'only two seats left'?
options: A. to inform customers about genuine technical limits on their servers
B. to rush shoppers into buying before checking competing offers
C. to reward returning users with last-minute price discounts
D. to comply with new European consumer transparency standards

steps: Đoạn 4: Gây lo lắng nhẹ khiến người mua bỏ qua bước so sánh giá kỹ lưỡng (cuts short careful price comparison).
Kết luận: Chọn B.

q26.text: Which statement best reflects the writer's conclusion in the final paragraph?
options: A. Consumers should stop purchasing luxury brands to avoid cognitive fatigue.
B. Digital stores should replace countdown clocks with higher fixed prices.
C. Rules should focus on stopping fake scarcity rather than outlawing prestige pricing.
D. Professional critics should test all online products before sale.

steps: Đoạn 5: Cấm hàng xa xỉ là bất khả thi; cơ quan quản lý nhắm vào việc buộc chứng minh cảnh báo hết hàng là thật.
Kết luận: Chọn C.
